questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Flyweight pattern?

options.text: Use sharing to support large numbers of fine-grained objects efficiently
Provide a simplified interface to a subsystem
Ensure a class has one instance

questions.explanation: Flyweight shares common state to save memory across many objects. Simplifying = Facade; one instance = Singleton; converting = Adapter.

questions.prompt: Match each kind of state to its description.

pairs.right: Shared, context-independent, stored in the flyweight
Unique per use, kept outside and passed in

questions.explanation: Intrinsic state is shared and immutable; extrinsic state (like coordinates) is unique per object and supplied from outside.

questions.prompt: Why must a flyweight's intrinsic state be immutable?

options.text: Because it is shared across many objects, so a change would corrupt all of them
Because it makes the objects singletons
Because extrinsic state can't exist otherwise

questions.explanation: Shared state that could change would affect every object referencing the flyweight, so it must be immutable.

questions.prompt: What does the flyweight factory guarantee?

options.text: That flyweights are reused — a new one is created only for a new combination of intrinsic state
That every request returns a brand-new object

questions.explanation: The factory caches and returns shared instances, creating one only when a genuinely new intrinsic combination appears.

questions.prompt: Flyweight's explicit goal is to save ____ when there are very many similar objects.
questions.explanation: It is the one GoF pattern whose stated purpose is efficient memory use across large numbers of objects.

questions.prompt: When is Flyweight the WRONG choice?

options.text: When you have only a modest number of objects, or each object's data is unique
When you have millions of objects sharing common data
When many objects share the same texture

questions.explanation: Flyweight only pays off at large scale with shared data; with few objects or all-unique state it just adds complexity.
